service_at_issue: Inpatient rehabilitation facility (IRF) services for five beneficiaries, March 2003 to May 2004
facts: This appeal involves IRF services provided by the appellant to five beneficiaries on various dates between March 2003 and May 2004. See Appendix A. The claims were initially paid between April 2003 and June 2004. Between October 2006 and April 2007, PRG Schultz, the Recovery Audit Contractor (RAC), informed the appellant that the claims had been selected for complex post- payment review.

The ALJ held a telephonic hearing in July 2008, for all of the claims. Dr. K.F., appellant’s Medical Director, testified. On August 8, 2008, the ALJ issued five hearing decisions. In each decision, the ALJ identified the issues before her as follows: Are the reopened initial determinations time-barred and, if not, were Medicare coverage criteria met for the IRF services at issue[?] If the reopenings are not time-barred and if Medicare coverage criteria are not met, should reimbursement be made under § 1879 of the [Social Security] Act and, if not, who, if anyone, is responsible for the non-covered charges?

(3) the ALJ erred by not applying special rules applicable to overpayments discovered after the third year after the initial determinations (that is, the appellant should be deemed without fault in creating the overpayments without evidence to the contrary, of which there is none);

(4) inasmuch as the appellant was without fault in creating the overpayments, there is no basis to recover any asserted overpayment; and (5) the appellant’s due process rights were violated by the RAC’s pecuniary interest in the outcome of the appeal.
outcome_note: The Council modified the ALJ decisions (the ALJ lacked authority to review the RAC's reopening and should have applied the three-year no-fault presumption, which was rebutted) but upheld the overpayments, provider liability and denial of waiver because the IRF services were not reasonable and necessary.
